headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 21 of the 28 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Western Maine. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Dry and seasonable weather to continue through early next week.
Dry cold front to bring cooler temperatures on Tuesday and Wednesday with dry weather now expected to continue through much of next week.

ALY.excerpt: ) High confidence in dry conditions persisting through at least the middle of next week.

GYX.excerpt: Dry weather continues areawide through the weekend and into next week. A cool and dry airmass will bring widespread overnight lows in the 20s tonight and Saturday night.

BUF.excerpt: ) Dry and tranquil weather is expected to continue through this Monday.

PHI.excerpt:
Elevated tide cycles persist due to Post-Tropical Cyclone Josephine well off the coast, resulting in widespread minor coastal flooding continuing in Ocean County, NJ and Sussex County, DE.
Frost and freeze impacts possible tonight and Saturday night where the growing season continues.

CTP.excerpt: ) Dry weather continues into the last week of October.

RLX.excerpt: ) Dry weather and comfortable temperatures for the next week. Dense valley fog will be possible each morning through the weekend as will areas of patchy frost across the mountains and northern lowlands.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Dry, with cold nights.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:23}} to {{t:48}}, mostly dry.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 39).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Friday 2:27 AM: "Dry and seasonable weather to continue through early next week."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and near-normal precipitation.

writeups.name: Massachusetts, Pennsylvania and West Virginia
writeups.title: Quiet and mild.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:29}} to {{t:55}}, mostly dry.
Snowshoe usually opens first here, around Nov 27. Nights stay too mild to make much snow this week.
NWS Albany forecasters, Friday 6:30 AM: ") High confidence in dry conditions persisting through at least the middle of next week."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans warmer than normal and slightly wetter than normal. Wet and mild often means rain below the summits.
